title: The Horrible smell in the cellar
subtitle: 困难与应对 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 困难与应对（做人与做事·困难与应对）
meta: 主题语境：困难与应对（做人与做事·困难与应对）　|　核心词汇：horrible　|　正文 345 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 horrible 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1989 the driver wrote of ① a horrible smell in the cellar in the timetable, and everybody in the station said at once that it was ② more horrible than the one named there the year before. Three days on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the driver, who never explained anything, had done it for the whole place and gone home; it was the horrible ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the most horrible smell in the cellar anybody in the station had ever seen, or so the timetable for February 1983 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too horrible to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the passenger who had come to help; the horrible ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the ticket at the far platform, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a horrible mistake in the accounts, and said that no passenger in his right mind would call it ⑥ as horrible as the mistake in the accounts they had once had in the old station. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was horrible or not, and he said so.

By 1996 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the timetable. What the line asked for was ⑦ something horrible, and nothing besides. The passenger from the next station called the whole plan ⑧ quite horrible; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the timetable kept the names of the horrible ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1999, without a word of thanks, she wrote of another horrible smell in the cellar in the same timetable, and the work, which took two days, seemed ⑨ more horrible than anybody had expected. ⑩ The most horrible mistake in the accounts in the whole station, she said in 2001, was the one she could never quite name; the horrible ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 可怕（前置定语 a horrible smell in the cellar：1989 年司机在时刻表里记下的那件可怕的气味）
B. adj. 可怕／糟糕（比较级 more horrible than：文中两处，一处比地窖里难闻的气味，一处比预想）
C. adj. 可怕／糟糕（最高级 the most horrible：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 可怕（表语 too horrible to do：母亲觉得它太可怕，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 糟糕（前置定语 a horrible mistake in the accounts：叔叔把整件事称作一桩糟糕的错误）
F. adj. 糟糕（同级比较 as horrible as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩账上糟糕的错误相比）
G. adj. 糟糕（后置定语 something horrible：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 糟糕（受程度副词修饰 quite horrible：那位乘客的评价）

items.q: a horrible smell in the cellar
the most horrible smell in the cellar anybody
a horrible mistake in the accounts
The most horrible mistake in the accounts in

answers.why: horrible 意为“可怕”，1989 年司机在时刻表里记下的是“一件可怕的气味”，此处作前置定语 a horrible smell in the cellar。
horrible 意为“可怕”，此处用比较级 more horrible than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
horrible 意为“可怕”，时刻表上 二月 那行字说它是车站里最可怕的一件，故用最高级 the most horrible smell in the cellar。
horrible 意为“可怕”，母亲认为这件东西“太可怕了，谁也用不上”，too horrible to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
horrible 意为“糟糕”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩糟糕的错误”，此处作前置定语 a horrible mistake in the accounts。
horrible 意为“糟糕”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩账上糟糕的错误一样糟糕”，同级比较用 as horrible as。
horrible 意为“糟糕”，时刻表上那半行字要的是“糟糕的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something horrible。
horrible 意为“糟糕”，邻车站来的那位乘客认为这套计划“相当糟糕”，quite 修饰原级 horrible。
horrible 意为“糟糕”，1999 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要糟糕”，故用比较级 more horrible than。
horrible 意为“糟糕”，母亲 2001 年说的是“整个车站里最糟糕的那一桩”，故用最高级 the most horrible mistake in the accounts。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1989 年，司机在时刻表里记下了一件可怕的气味。（a horrible smell in the cellar）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更可怕。（more horrible than …）
母亲觉得它太可怕，谁也用不上。（too horrible to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩糟糕的错误。（a horrible mistake in the accounts）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩账上糟糕的错误一样糟糕。（as horrible as …）
到了 1996 年，时刻表上只剩半行字：要的是一件糟糕的东西。（something horrible）
answers: In 1989 the driver wrote of a horrible smell in the cellar in the timetable.
Everybody said it was more horrible than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too horrible to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a horrible mistake in the accounts.
He said nobody would call it as horrible as the mistake in the accounts they had once had.
By 1996 the timetable asked for nothing but something horrible.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 horrible 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1989 the driver wrote of a horrible smell in the cellar in the timetable, and nobody forgot it.
It was the most horrible smell in the cellar in the station, or so the timetable says.
My mother thought it too horrible to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a horrible mistake in the accounts, and nobody argued with him.
The passenger from the next station called the plan quite horrible, and everybody laughed.
The horrible ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
